subject: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot

Jordan — following up from the call yesterday. Attached is the revised Master Capacity Purchase (rev3) and the demand forecast you shared. Key ask: Skyline needs a binding reservation for 24xH200 equivalent, but due to supply constraints would like the right to transparently fall back to a mixed H100 pool for up to 25% of token-hours during a 90-day ramp window.

We can support that with a temporary exception to our standard Dedicated SKU policy if leadership signs off on: 1) a tiered overage cap (no more than 40% premium on excess usage in month 1, then 70% premium month 2–3), 2) an approved performance-validation run prior to go-live, and 3) a one-time pilot discount of 15% applied to the first three months of committed spend.

Deal details:
- Deal ID: DEAL-8943
- Committed capacity: 24 units (12-month term)
- Pilot window: 90 days of mixed-fleet allowance

Attachments: Skyline_MCP_MA_rev3.docx, capacity-forecast.csv

Requested action: Can someone on Exec/Deal Desk confirm approval for the above exception (GPU-family swap allowance + tiered overage pricing + pilot discount)? If approved we will prepare a redline and DocuSign packet for Skyline.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

-- Attachment stubs: Skyline_MCP_MA_rev3.docx (28 KB), capacity-forecast.csv (14 KB)
From: Jordan Mills <jmills@skylinehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot

Ben — thanks for the fast follow. A couple of points from our side before we can accept a mixed-fleet approach:

1) H100 fallback: our latency-sensitive inference paths are cert-critical. We need a written SLA on p99 token latency degradation when fallback occurs and a guaranteed rollback path to H200-only within 72 hours if performance thresholds are missed.
2) Overage pricing: the tiers you listed are acceptable in principle, but procurement needs an explicit cap on monthly spend growth attributable to fallback. Can Redwood commit to an absolute monthly overage ceiling for the pilot?
3) Timeline: we need the contract signed and the validation run complete before Oct 15 to meet our internal launch.

Cc'ing procurement so legal can review the redline when you share it.

Jordan Mills
VP, Platform Engineering — Skyline Health
jmills@skylinehealth.com

-- Procurement contact: procurement@skylinehealth.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot

Team — forwarding the Skyline thread (below). Summary and my recommendation: approve a constrained exception to allow a mixed H200/H100 footprint for ramp months, with the following guardrails: 

- Discount: reduce proposed pilot discount to 12% (from 15%) and apply only to committed units (first 3 billing cycles).
- Overage tiers: keep the proposed premium schedule, but add an absolute monthly overage cap of $120k for the pilot period; any overage above that must be escalated and paused.
- Rollback SLA: yes to a 72-hour rollback commitment; require an automated rollback trigger tied to p99 latency > 1.5x baseline measured in Redwood Console for two consecutive hours.
- Validation: schedule a 48-hour performance-validation run by Redwood infra engineers; success criteria documented in HubSpot (see link).
- Reservation hold: place a 14-day soft reservation hold (no invoice) while legal redlines are finalized.
- Opt-out: allow Skyline a 60-day pilot opt-out with 30 days' notice.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456/DEAL-8943
I prepared a short redline summary (redline_summary.txt) — attaching now.

If we greenlight with those guards I recommend Lauren sign off and Finance prepare a one-time commit credit equal to 5% of month-1 committed spend. Ben, can you confirm you can turn around the DocuSign with those items and the redline?

Mina Haddad
Head of Sales Ops – Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

-- Attachment stub: redline_summary.txt (3 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot

+1 to Mina's recommendation with the following amendment: require a one-time invoice-level commit credit (applied before any overage) equal to 5% of the first invoice and a technical validation plan to be executed by our infra team within 7 calendar days of signature. Validation must include KV cache retention tests and a 24-hour steady-state throughput run at the forecast 90th percentile. If the validation fails, the mixed-fleet allowance is suspended until remediation.

Also recommend we log the fallback behavior as an SLA event in Redwood Console (tagged for Skyline) so CS and SRE can monitor automatically. If Finance can confirm the credit treatment, I approve.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product – Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Tiered overage bridge & GPU fleet exception for Skyline pilot

Approved. Lauren sign-off for the temporary mixed-fleet exception and tiered overage structure, subject to Karthik's validation plan and the one-time commit credit (5% first invoice). Finance Ops — please prepare the credit and apply against the first invoice; note the 14-day reservation hold Mina requested.

Ben — proceed to finalize the redline, update DocuSign with the guardrails, and coordinate the validation run. Loop me in once DocuSign is ready for signature.

Lauren Bishop
